project.name: ColimaUI
project.description: Desktop and browser GUI for Colima, Docker, Kubernetes, Lima virtual machines and AI diagnostics.

modules.name: frontend
modules.description: Svelte pages, shared components, rune stores and the dual-mode API client.

modules.name: backend
modules.description: Rust/Tauri application, Axum HTTP routes, shared commands, adapters, services and CLI binaries.

testing.commandsNote: Node.js >=22.22.2 is required. npm commands match package scripts, Tauri config and CI; README also documents pnpm, and both lockfiles exist, so no startup package-manager preference is selected. Rust integration tests may require Docker, Colima or Trivy and may carry #[ignore]; choose their prerequisites before running them. Run the repository's quality gates before committing or pushing; see README.md.

referenceDocs.purpose: Before changing application boundaries or transport behavior — dual-mode architecture and data flow
Before editing Svelte pages, shared controls, stores or styling — frontend conventions and ownership
Before changing Rust commands, HTTP routes, adapters or services — backend patterns and validation ownership
Before changing HTTP endpoints or client contracts — API reference and request behavior
Before changing AI diagnostics, tools, knowledge bank or command sandbox — AI system behavior
Before adding topology node kinds or actions — topology design rules and interaction boundaries
Before changing telemetry or outbound data — data disclosure and transmission behavior
Before planning changes or tracing entry points — source-derived project structure, runtime and delivery
Before editing backend behavior — source-derived request, validation, persistence and asynchronous patterns
Before editing frontend behavior — source-derived composition, state, input and navigation conventions
Before changing visual styles or shared controls — source-derived design tokens, components and assets
Before reviewing project changes — source-backed quality gates and local review rules
Before changing resource lifecycle or safety rules — executable domain concepts, ownership and invariants
Before changing boundary tests — source-derived harness, isolation, prerequisites and assertions
Before changing fixture or sample-data setup — actual loaders, corpus generators and bootstrap ownership

surfaces.notes: Vite serves the frontend; application operations also need the Rust backend running. The HTTP client discovers API ports 11420-11429. See vite.config.ts, src/lib/api/client.ts and docs/architecture.md.

Requires frontend dependencies, Rust/Tauri build prerequisites and native UI inspection. Backend resource actions additionally depend on the relevant local runtime tools. See README.md and src-tauri/tauri.conf.json.

surfaces.runner: HTTP client against the running Axum server
surfaces.notes: Start the application to host the server; discover its actual port in 11420-11429. Health is unauthenticated; protected operations use the local API-token reference described in src-tauri/src/auth.rs. Never copy token values into evidence. See src-tauri/src/api_server.rs and docs/api.md.

colimaui is declared with required-features = [cli] in src-tauri/Cargo.toml; cui is a Rust binary in src-tauri/src/bin/cui.rs and needs the running backend for requests. Rust and native build prerequisites are required. No full verification suite or accepted output baseline is declared.
